newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen seen bearish on firmer economic data.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen seen bearish on firmer economic data.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen interest rate futures stayed defensive on Thursday after better-than-expected results from the Bank of Japan's quarterly business survey.
The tankan on Wednesday triggered sharp declines, and led to more follow-through selling by Japanese banks on Thursday.
"Some Japanese banks are still selling into rallies," a dealer with a European commission house said.
He noted the mood was also cautious ahead of industrial output figures on Friday, which were expected to be positive.
December Euroyen futures were at 99.03 by 1115 GMT, down from its IMM close at 99.04 on volume of 12,210 lots.
The fall in Euroyen futures after the tankan factored in a possible Japanese interest rate cut, dealers said.
But on closer scrutiny, the tankan also threw up a less bullish scenario for the non-manufacturing sector, they said.
Japanese government bond's (JGB) experienced a mild revival after plunging on the tankan on Wednesday.
Dealers said a bottom may have been reached for now, as those who sold heavily were seen short covering especially after the stock market eased.
"There's still more room for downside in the long end, possibly 122.70, but it should be supported for now," a dealer with a Japanese brokerage said.
The SIMEX September JGB futures contract ended at 123.31, up 0.04 points.
Eurodollar futures traded sideways in lacklustre conditions, dampened by weaker U.S. treasuries overnight and Euroyen.
The market was expected to focus soon on employment reports next week, as concerns about inflationary pressures continued to cap rises.
December Eurodollars closed at 93.940 against their IMM close at 93.945, and March at 93.860 against 93.855.
